nodes.label: Sergin Modular Monolith
nodes.rationale: .NET 10 modular monolith on PostgreSQL, DDD + Clean Architecture with per-feature vertical slices. Split across three repos (MeterMinder root/hostable, SharedKernel and UserAccess as submodules) so each piece has its own lifecycle, while relative submodule paths keep every ProjectReference resolving unchanged.

nodes.label: Sergin.MeterMinder.Hosts.All
nodes.rationale: The single runnable host: a ~20-line Program.cs that builds IReadOnlyCollection<ISerginModule> and hands it to the presentation bootstrap before and after Build(). Adding a module costs one collection element plus two ProjectReferences.

nodes.label: Dropped Web API Host
nodes.rationale: Sergin.MeterMinder.Hosts.WebApi.All was deliberately deleted because the Blazor UI dispatches to module handlers in-process through MediatR, so the HTTP hop bought nothing. Everything below the host still compiles: the endpoint layer is live-but-unhosted, not dead, so restoring an API is a ~20-line Program.cs rather than a rewrite.

nodes.label: MeterMinder Module (schema mm)
nodes.rationale: Head-End System (HES) for smart electricity/gas/water meters — device communication and data collection. Maps to Postgres schema mm.

nodes.label: UserAccess Module (schema ua)
nodes.rationale: Identity and access module, mounted as a git submodule and embed-only (no solution file or Directory.*.props of its own). Its Users slice is the canonical reference implementation for every new feature.

nodes.label: AddSerginCore
nodes.rationale: The presentation-agnostic half of both bootstraps: MediatR scanning, pipeline behaviors, event dispatcher, IDbConnectionFactory, IUserContext, localizer, and the module.AddServices loop. It deliberately does NOT register IUserContextFactory, because an API host derives the user from HttpContext while the UI host derives it from configuration. Because both bootstraps call it internally, one process cannot call both without double-registering every DbContext and handler.

nodes.label: AddSerginWebUi / UseSerginWebUiAsync
nodes.rationale: Blazor bootstrap in Sergin.SharedKernel.Hosts.WebUi: Razor Components with interactive server rendering, AddSerginBlazorKit, DevUserOptions binding, ConfiguredUserContextFactory, AddSerginCore, and a SerginUiModuleCatalog. UseSerginWebUiAsync runs the route-prefix guard, migrates modules (Development only), then maps Razor components with the catalog's routable assemblies.

nodes.label: AddSerginWebApi / UseSerginWebApiAsync
nodes.rationale: Web API bootstrap: OpenAPI, IHttpContextAccessor, HttpContext-derived InternalUserContextFactory, then AddSerginCore; UseSerginWebApiAsync migrates modules and maps each ISerginWebApiModule's endpoints under MapGroup(module.Schema). Compiled but currently unhosted, kept working on purpose.

nodes.label: AddServiceDefaults (Aspire ServiceDefaults)
nodes.rationale: Wires OpenTelemetry, health checks, resilience, and service discovery. Aspire here is ServiceDefaults plus a dashboard container only — there is no AppHost project anywhere in the repo, and local orchestration is Docker Compose. Earlier prose calling it 'Aspire for local orchestration' was an overstatement.

nodes.label: ISerginModule
nodes.rationale: Core module contract exposing Schema, ApplicationAssembly, AddServices, and MigrateAsync. Two capability interfaces extend it, and one class per module implements every capability the module exposes so hosts can pick what they run.

nodes.label: ISerginWebApiModule
nodes.rationale: Adds MapEndpoints(RouteGroupBuilder) with per-aggregate Map<X>Endpoints(). Nothing calls it today, but keeping it implemented is exactly what makes re-adding an API host cheap.

nodes.label: ISerginWebUiModule
nodes.rationale: Adds UiAssembly (the Blazor RCL holding routable components — never ApplicationAssembly, which is deliberately UI-free) and NavItems.

nodes.label: SerginNavItem
nodes.rationale: (Label, Href, Icon, Order) record where Icon is a plain string, so the contract leaf stays free of any UI library even though modules pass MudBlazor Icons.Material constants into it.

nodes.label: IUserContextFactory
nodes.rationale: The one registration left host-shaped. Every host must register its own implementation before calling AddSerginCore; a host that forgets fails to resolve IUserContext. The API bootstrap uses HttpContext-derived InternalUserContextFactory, the UI bootstrap uses config-driven ConfiguredUserContextFactory.

nodes.label: ISerginUiDispatcher
nodes.rationale: Blazor pages must inject this, never ISender/IMediator: in Blazor Server 'scoped' is the SignalR circuit's lifetime, so a directly resolved ISender would share one DbContext for as long as the tab is open (unbounded change tracker, stale first-level-cache reads, concurrent-operation errors). ScopedSerginUiDispatcher opens a fresh IServiceScope per send and is correctly registered as a singleton since it holds only the root IServiceScopeFactory.

nodes.label: IUiErrorPresenter
nodes.rationale: Two shapes: Notify() for a transient snackbar on list pages and submits, Present() into a SerginProblem field rendered by SerginProblemPanel on detail pages where the failure is the whole page. MudUiErrorPresenter maps errors through the same SerginProblemFactory the API uses, so both surfaces render identical text for a given error.Code.

nodes.label: DevUserOptions
nodes.rationale: Bound from Sergin:DevUser and registered with ValidateOnStart plus a custom DevUserOptionsValidator that delegates to DevUserOptions.Validate(out string failure). The custom validator (rather than a .Validate(predicate) lambda) exists so startup failure names the offending key AND value instead of a generic 'options validation failed'.

nodes.label: Development-Only Host Guard
nodes.rationale: AddSerginWebUi throws on its first line outside Development because the host has no authentication at all — every request runs as one configured Sergin:DevUser. This is why ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: Development in docker-compose.yml is mandatory, not merely convenient. The dev user grants only the two permissions the UI exercises; permission.mm.manufacturers.read is deliberately withheld because no Manufacturers UI exists.

nodes.label: SerginApplicationOptions
nodes.rationale: Binds Sergin:ApplicationName and lives in Sergin.SharedKernel.Presentation so it stays presentation-agnostic and a future API host could reuse it for an OpenAPI title. SerginMainLayout emits it as a fallback PageTitle only — HeadOutlet keeps the last title rendered and the body renders after the layout, so each page's own PageTitle wins. There is no title composition because Blazor has no built-in mechanism for it.

nodes.label: Route Prefix Startup Guard
nodes.rationale: Every module page route must start with /{schema}/. UseSerginWebUiAsync reflects over each UiAssembly for exported IComponents carrying [Route] and throws at startup listing offenders. A guard exists rather than central prefixing because @page templates are compile-time constants — there is no MapGroup(schema) equivalent for Razor routes.

nodes.label: PermissionCheckPipelineBehavior
nodes.rationale: First MediatR behavior in order: enforces [RequiredPermissions] on any IBaseCommand (covering commands and queries) against IUserContext, returning Error.Forbidden() on failure.

nodes.label: ValidationPipelineBehavior
nodes.rationale: Second behavior: runs an optional FluentValidation IValidator<TRequest> if one is registered. FluentValidation is wired but no AbstractValidator exists in the codebase yet.

nodes.label: RequiredPermissions Attribute
nodes.rationale: permission.<schema>.<resource>.<action> applied per slice. Opt-in, not universal — its absence on an existing handler is not an oversight to fix incidentally.

nodes.label: List-Query Permission Gap
nodes.rationale: List features have no dedicated request record — handlers implement IListQueryHandler<TItem> directly against the shared generic ListQuery<TItem>, so there is no type to attribute with [RequiredPermissions]. This is a structural gap in the shared generic, not an inconsistently applied convention; authorizing a list feature would require introducing a feature-specific list-query type, for which no precedent exists.

nodes.label: CQRS Read/Write Split
nodes.rationale: Writes flow endpoint → MediatR ICommand → handler → domain AggregateRoot factory → EF repository → IUnitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync, each module owning its own unit of work. Reads bypass EF entirely, going through I<Feature>QueryRepository backed by raw SQL. Queries live under Commands/ folders, not a separate Queries/ folder.

nodes.label: IDbConnectionFactory Raw-SQL Read Side
nodes.rationale: Each query method opens its own connection (never shared or injected). SQL is a raw string literal with snake_case columns aliased to the response record's exact property casing so Dapper's binder matches. List queries batch a count and a paged select through one QueryMultipleAsync and read both off the same GridReader. Not-found is bare Error.NotFound() because ApiProblemResults localizes on error.Code, so per-feature codes would need localization resources first.

nodes.label: Per-Module Clean Architecture Layering
nodes.rationale: Domain / Application / Infrastructure / Infrastructure.Data / Presentation.WebApi / optional Presentation.Blazor / composition root, enforcing dependency direction. Aggregates use a private parameterless constructor plus a static Create factory with object-initializer syntax, Guid.CreateVersion7() for IDs, and strongly-typed IDs declared as trailing sealed records in the same file as their aggregate. The Presentation.Blazor RCL references .Application but never .Infrastructure — pages reach handlers through MediatR only.

nodes.label: TreatWarningsAsErrors Build Constraint
nodes.rationale: Directory.Build.props sets TreatWarningsAsErrors, AnalysisMode=All, SonarAnalyzer.CSharp, and EnforceCodeStyleInBuild, so any analyzer, style, or nullable warning fails the build. Code must pass analysis cleanly the first time.

nodes.label: Central Package Management
nodes.rationale: Directory.Packages.props holds every version as a PackageVersion entry; PackageReference items carry no Version attribute or the build fails with NU1008. New packages are referenced version-less and added alphabetically to the central list.

nodes.label: Static Web Assets Double ProjectReference
nodes.rationale: Static web assets (_content/...) propagate only through projects importing Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets. The module composition roots are plain Microsoft.NET.Sdk, so the chain host → composition root → RCL breaks silently at the middle hop (ResolveReferencedProjectsStaticWebAssetsConfiguration probes with SkipNonexistentTargets=true, so nothing warns). Without a direct RCL reference MudBlazor's CSS 404s and the UI renders unstyled — verified empirically. A UI-bearing module therefore needs two ProjectReferences, not one.

nodes.label: Markup-Only .razor Rule
nodes.rationale: Every line of C# lives in the matching .razor.cs partial class because code inside an @code block compiles through the Razor source generator into output the analyzer pipeline does not gate — an unaudited hole in a repo where analyzers gate every other line. There are zero @code blocks today.

nodes.label: SharedKernel and UserAccess Submodules
nodes.source_location: ## SharedKernel and UserAccess are separate repos, mounted as submodules
nodes.rationale: Both are mounted at the same relative paths they occupied before the three-repo split, which is what lets every ProjectReference resolve without path rewrites — MSBuild's Directory.Build.props auto-discovery walks the physical directory tree and does not care that a submodule boundary sits partway up. SharedKernel builds standalone; UserAccess is embed-only and needs a host repo to compile.

nodes.label: Per-Module EF Core Migrations
nodes.rationale: Each module owns its DbContext and migrations, so --project points at that module's Infrastructure.Data project. Migrations apply automatically at startup only in Development. Gotcha: design-time factories load only appsettings.Development.json — not env vars or user secrets — so `migrations add` scaffolds fine without a connection string but `database update` from the CLI will not connect.

nodes.label: SerginWebApiFactory Test Fixture
nodes.rationale: One shared factory per test collection, starting a Testcontainers PostgreSql container in InitializeAsync and setting the connection-string env var before the host builds (a ConfigureWebHost override runs too late). Despite the WebApi in its name it is presentation-agnostic. Write-path tests dispatch in-process via ISerginUiDispatcher rather than HTTP, because dispatching opens a fresh DI scope per send so the read genuinely round-trips through Postgres instead of the writing DbContext's change tracker. A second host would need a separate test project — two host Programs in the global namespace collide as CS0433.

nodes.label: Present-but-Unused Domain Events
nodes.rationale: AggregateRoot supports Raise/DomainEvents/ClearDomainEvents and EventDispatcherInterceptor dispatches them on SaveChanges, but no aggregate calls Raise today. Ardalis.GuardClauses and RowVersion are in the same present-but-unused state — infrastructure to follow when needed, not evidence that events already flow.

nodes.label: Strongly-Typed IDs and Value Converters
nodes.rationale: Record wrappers mapped to columns via EF ValueConverters following a fixed skeleton (with a null-ternary variant for nullable value objects). The misspelling DeviceIntenralId is the real type name and must be matched, not corrected.

nodes.label: Missing FK-Existence Check on Write
nodes.rationale: CreateDeviceCommandHandler inserts a Device referencing ManufacturerId without checking the manufacturer exists, so a bad ID surfaces as a raw Postgres FK-violation exception rather than an ErrorOr result. This is the current state of the only cross-aggregate FK, explicitly not an established pattern to replicate.

nodes.label: ErrorOr Result Convention
nodes.rationale: Handlers return ErrorOr<T> (globally imported); endpoints call .ToApiResult() to convert to an IResult/ProblemDetails, and Blazor pages route the same errors through IUiErrorPresenter.

nodes.label: Unwired Sort/Filter/Search Plumbing
nodes.rationale: ListQuery carries Term, Filtering, and Sorting, but ToListQuery forwards only Term, SendListAsync forwards none, and no query repository reads any of them (hardcoded ORDER BY id). A UI control bound to any of them would silently do nothing, which is worse than omitting it — so list pages are paging-only. Wiring them through is a read-side feature, not a UI change.
